Asiahaslongbeenascientificfocus,whichisbeneficialforawiderangeofgeologicalstudies,forexample,
Acceptedarticleonline25JUN2020 platetectonics(Metcalfe,2013;Torsvik&Cocks,2013),globalclimatechange(Goddérisetal.,2017),andthe
end‐Permian mass extinction (Shen et al., 2019). The Indochina Block is considered as one of the major
blocksthatriftedanddriftedfromthenorthernmarginofeasternGondwanaandisinterpretedtobeinclose
relationship with the South China Block during the early Paleozoic (Metcalfe, 1996, 2013; Torsvik &
Cocks,2013,2017).Althoughgreatendeavorhasbeenmadetodepictthesuccessivedispersionofeastern
Gondwana blocks, it is still a tentative restoration for the Paleozoic period (Metcalfe, 2013; Stampfli &
Borel,2002;Torsvik&Cocks,2013,2017),whichismainlyattributedtothepaucityofreliablepaleomag-
netic data. For instance, Torsvik and Cocks (2013) considered the separation of South China‐Indochina
(or Annamia) from the Arabian‐Indian margin of Gondwana as early as the Early Ordovician, while
Metcalfe(2013)interpretedtheseparationhappenedattheIndian‐AustralianmarginofGondwanaduring
theMiddleDevonian.TheinitialoccurrenceofpelagicradiolarianchertsandophiolitesinthePaleo‐Tethys
suture zone suggest that the separation of South China‐Indochina‐North Qiangtang from Gondwana
occurredsincetheEarly‐MiddleDevonian(Lietal.,1995,2016;Metcalfe,2013;Zhong,1998).Thisinterpre-
tationissupportedpaleomagneticallythroughfittingapparentpolarwanderpathswhichindicatedtherift-
ing of South China‐Indochina from Gondwana occurred during ~400–385 Ma (Xian et al., 2019).
ConsideringthePermian‐TriassicdriftinghistoryoftheNorthQiangtangandIndochinablockshasbeen
schematically described (Ma et al., 2019; Song et al., 2017; Yan et al., 2018, 2019), reconstructing the

TobetterreconstructthedispersionhistoryoftheeasternGondwanablocks,soastoprovideinformationfor
understanding the mechanism, we report a paleomagnetic study on the Carboniferous strata in the
IndochinaBlockinsouthernmostYunnanProvinceofChina.
2. Geologic Settings andSampling
LocatingintheSoutheastAsianPeninsula,theIndochinaBlock(orAnnamia)isadjacenttotheSouthChina
andSibumasublocksattheJinshaJiang‐AilaoShan‐SongMasuturetothenortheastandtheChangning‐
Menglian‐Chianglai‐Chiangmai‐Inthanan suture belt to the west, respectively (Figure 1a). In the Simao
Terrane,thenorthernpartofIndochina,theCarboniferousstrataarerarelyoutcroppedbecausemostareas
arecoveredbyMesozoicsedimentarystrata.TheCarboniferousstrataintheMengxingarea,southernmost
ofYunnanChina,weresubdividedintotheLower,MiddleandUpperSeriesbyBGMRYP(1976),following
previouschronostratigraphicalschemeduring1950sto1970s.TheLowerSeriesconsistsofgraymudstone,
siltstone, and sandstone, including fossils such as Neuropteris gigantea, Kansuella maximus, and
Dibunophyllumcf.burbinatum,whichcorrespondstotheMississippianSubsystem.TheMiddleSeriescon-
sists mainly of gray bioclastic limestone and merely of shalestone, containing Fusulina schllwieni,
Fusulinella bocki, and Profusulinella deprati fossils, which corresponds to the Lower (Bashkirian) and
Middle(Moscovian)StagesofthePennsylvanianSubsystem.TheUpperSeriesconsistsofshalestone,mud-
stone, and bioclastic limestone, including fossils such as Triticites cf. parvulus, Quasifusulina sp. and

Schwagerina cf. valgaris, which corresponds to the Upper Stage of the Pennsylvanian Subsystem. These
strataarefaultorunconformablycontactedwiththePermianandTriassicstrata.
Becausenaturaloutcropsarefewinthevirgintropicalforeststhisarea,samplescanonlybecollectedalong
theNationalRoadG213linkingtheMengxingvillageandMenglacounty(Figure1b).Samplesforpaleo-
magnetic analyses were collected from the Middle Carboniferous limestone strata, which correspond to
the Bashkirian and Moscovian Stages (~323–307 Ma). Paleomagnetic samples were drilled in 18 sites
(MX6–MX23)distributedinacompositeanticlineusingaportablewatercoolingandgasolinepowereddril-
lingmachineandorientedusingmagneticandsuncompasses,thelocalmagneticanomalyisestimatedtobe
about−1°.
3. RockMagnetic andPetrographic Analyses: Methods andResults
Todetectthecompositionofmagneticminerals,IRMs(isothermalremanentmagnetizations)ofstandard
specimensaremeasuredstepwiselyfrom1to2,500mTusinga2G‐760cryogenicmagnetometeraftermag-
netizedwithapulsemagnetometer.IRMsincreasegraduallywiththeappliedfieldanddonotreachsatura-
tionevenat2.5T,fromwhichthreecoercivitycomponentsarerevealed(Figures2a–2h;Heslopetal.,2002).
The average values of lower‐coercivity (B ), intermedium‐coercivity (B ), and high‐coercivity (B )
L½ M½ H½
componentsareinterpretedtobe50–80,300–500,and>1,000mT(Figures2e–2h).Tofurtherunderstand
thethreecomponents,detailedstepwisethermaldemagnetizationwassubjectedtoX‐Y‐Zaxes,whichwere
magnetizedwith100,500,and2,500mTusingapulsemagnetometer(Lowrie,1990).Thesoftcomponent
(coercivity<100mT)iserasedgraduallyfromroomtemperatureto~600°Candisinterpretedtobethesig-
nalofmagnetite.Themediumcomponent(coercivitybetween100and500mT)ofspecimensMX6‐1,MX8‐
7,andMX18‐3droppedsignificantlyat~300°Cto350°Candwasinterpretedtobecarriedprobablybypyr-
rhotite (Dekkers,1989). Nosignal of pyrrhotite is recognized in specimenMX23‐2. The hardcomponent
(coercivitybetween500and2,500mT)dropssharplyfromroomtemperatureto100°Cor120°Candisinter-
pretedtobethetransitionfromgoethitetomaghemite(Figures2i–2l).

ciumcarbonates.Theacetatebufferisamixtureof2MCH COOHand1MCH COONawithavolumeratio 3 3

titeswithinhexagonal‐plateshapearealsoobserved(Figures3d–3f).Theperfectlypreservedcrystalforms
implythatthegoethiteandpyrrhotiteareverylikelysecondaryauthigenicminerals.

5. Discussions
5.1. PaleopositionoftheIndochinaBlockDuringLatePaleozoic
InthepaleogeographicmodelsofScotese(2004)andMetcalfe(2013),itisdepictedthattheIndochinaBlock
locatednorthofSouthChinaandoutboardofSibumasuintheAustralianmarginofGondwanaduringthe
early Paleozoic and did not separate from Gondwana until the Middle Devonian. However, Torsvik and
Cocks (2013) suggested that the Indochina located south of South China and outboard of Qiangtang in
theArabia‐IndianmarginofGondwana,whichissupportedindirectlythroughanalyzingagedistributions
and Hf isotope compositions of detrital zircons from Indochina as well as those from Qiangtang,
Tethys‐Himalaya and western Cathaysia (Usuki et al., 2013). At the same time, some other authors also

supposed that the Indochina might be located outboard the Sibumasu
BlockintheIndianmarginofGondwana(Kangetal.,2019).Obviously,
furtherreliablepaleomagneticdataareneededtoconstraintthepaleopo-
sitionofSouthChina‐IndochinaduringtheearlyPaleozoic.
During the late Paleozoic, because of the paucity of quantitative paleo-
magneticdata,theIndochina Blockwassupposedtowanderacrossthe
paleo‐equator,backandforth,basedonevidencesofwarm‐waterfossils
(Metcalfe,2013;Scotese,2004;Torsvik&Cocks,2013).TheSouthChina
Block was connected to Gondwana from the (pre‐)Cambrian to Late
Devonian(Yangetal.,2004)anditsseparationfromGondwanawasinter-
preted to be ~400–385 Ma through fitting apparent polar wander paths
(Xianetal.,2019).Recently,Xianetal.(2019)suggestedthattheSouth
China‐Indochina had broken up with Gondwana by latest
Devonian(~360Ma),andthebranchofPaleo‐TethysOceanbetweenthem
wasaswideas~1,600kmlatitudinally(Figures6aand6b).Considering
thattheLateDevoniantoEarlyPermianpositionofSouthChinawascon-
strainedpaleomagneticallytobeattheequatorialarea(Wuetal.,1998;
Zhangetal.,2001,2015),the~180°clockwiserotationofSouthChinadur-
ing the Carboniferous which implies significant synchronal northward
transition, as illustrated in Scotese (2004), is not consistent with these
paleomagneticstudies.
Inthisstudy,thepaleomagneticdata(Table1andFigure5)providetwo
plausible positions at a latitude of ~18.4° in the Northern or Southern
Hemispheres for the Indochina in the middle Carboniferous (~315 Ma)
Figure 7.Paleolatitude variation of Indochina, North Qiangtang, South because of the symmetry of geomagnetic dipole field. We prefer that
China(Huangetal.,2018;Wuetal.,1998),andthatofEurasiaandIndia
theIndochinaBockwaslocatedat18.4±4.0°Sbecauseoftworeasons: ofGondwana(Torsviketal.,2012).Referencesofdata:Indochina(Achache
&Courtillot,1985;Chietal.,2016;Yanetal.,2017,2018;Yang&
first,itspaleobiogeographic(Audley‐Charles,1983)andlithofaciespaleo-
Besse,2001)andNorthQiangtang(Chengetal.,2012,2013;Huang geographic (Helmcke, 1985) relationships with North Qiangtang has
etal.,1992;Songetal.,2012,2015,2017;Yangetal.,2016). long been documented (Li, 1987; Li et al., 1995; Metcalfe, 1996, 2013),
and the Late Carboniferous‐Permian northward transition of North
QiangtangfromtheSouthernHemispheretotheNorthernHemispherehasbeenreconstructedpaleomag-
netically(Chengetal.,2013;Maetal.,2019;Songetal.,2017;Yangetal.,2016).Therefore,itisreasonable
to consider that Late Carboniferous Indochina was located at the Southern Hemisphere; second, the
breakupoftheSouthChinaBlockfromGondwanaduringtheMiddle‐LateDevonianwasprovedbypaleo-
magnetic studies (Xian et al., 2019; Yang et al., 2004), which is consistent with the initial occurrence of
pelagic radiolarian cherts and ophiolites in the Paleo‐Tethys suture zone (Li et al., 1995, 2016;
Metcalfe, 2013; Zhong, 1998). Therefore, it is unlikely that the South China‐Indochina (or Annamia)
blocksriftedfromGondwanaduring the EarlyOrdovician,transitedtothe NorthernHemisphereby the
LateOrdovicianandsubsequentlytheIndochinamovedbacktotheSouthernHemispherebyseparating
from South China during the Late Devonian to Late Carboniferous times, as illustrated in Torsvik and
Cocks (2013). Moreover, the Middle‐Late Devonian breakup of South China‐Indochina from Gondwana
wasadoptedintheupdatedreconstructionsbyTorsvikandCocks(2017).Therefore,itisdifficulttoimage
that the Indochina Block transited to and moved back alone from the Northern Hemisphere quickly
during the Carboniferous‐Permian period, while South China is stationary in the equatorial area (Wu
etal.,1998; Zhang etal.,2001,2015).In this case, ratherthana southward drift,a northward driftfrom
~18.4°S in the middle Carboniferous, through ~16.3°S in the Early‐Middle Permian (Yan et al., 2018) to
6.4°S in the Late Permian (Chi et al., 2016) is an easier model to depict the movement of Indochina
(Figure7).

6. Conclusions
Different magnetic components were isolated from the middle Carboniferous limestones after thermal
demagnetizations.TheChRM(HTC)passedreversalandfoldtestsandisverylikelyaprimaryrecord.The
MTCisinterpretedtobesynfoldingrecordsofpyrrhotitesandtheLTCisidentifiedtobeagoethite‐carried
viscousremanenceofthepresentgeomagneticfield.Theinferredmagneticmineralsareconfirmedusing
SEMinmagneticallyconcentratedsamples.Magneticconcentrationondissolvedlimestonesusingmixed
solutionsofCH COOHandCH COONaispracticalinpreparingsamplesforidentifyingmagneticminerals.
3 3
ThisstudyprovidesamiddleCarboniferous(~315Ma)paleomagneticpoleof76.1°S/181.3°E(A =4.0°, 95
N = 14) from limestones in southernmostYunnan of China. This new pole indicatesthat the Indochina
Blockwaslocatedat18.4±4.0°S.ThemiddleCarboniferous‐EarlyPermianisfoundtobearelativelyquiet
tectonicperiodfortheIndochinaBlock,aswellastheNorthQiangtangandSouthChinablocks.Asequen-
tialrapidtransitionoftheNorthQiangtang,Indochina,andSouthChinablockswasrecognized,whichis
coevalwiththeriftingofCimmerianterranesfromGondwana.
